original.title: 🎬 01 · Screenwriting Foundations
original.deliverable: 10 observations · 4 practice scenes · 1 screenplay (3–5 pages) · 6-shot directing plan

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Watch [Anatomy of a Screenplay](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6PLSJBTzaGw) (about 22m); spend the remaining 8m noting scene heading, action line, character cue and one unanswered question.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Completed an extended comparison of roughly 10 screenplay pages with approximately the first 5 minutes of *Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse*.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Write two short field notes from behavior you actually saw today. Keep them in your writing notes, not the Session Vault; that archive is for substantial creative work.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Re-read the two notes. Keep visible actions factual and label any motive as a possibility. Leave routine notes out of the Session Vault.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Write from memory the Hangul letters you know; review ㄹ and ㅇ; write and sound out 가 나 다 라 마 바 사 자 아 오 twice.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Watch/review [Anatomy of a Screenplay](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6PLSJBTzaGw) on scene headings and action descriptions. Write one correct example of each.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Read 1–3 opening pages of [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf); watch the matching scene in the [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI). Note one written action translated into images.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Add two real-life field notes to the same writing document. For each, note the visible action, possible want, obstacle, and one filmable detail. Keep them out of the Session Vault.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Check #3–4: remove any guesses from the "Observed" field.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Review 10 familiar Hangul blocks; practise vowels ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ; copy and read 10 blocks twice.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Study [How to Write Great Scenes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TukzX6R57Y), conflict chapter (03:08–08:21). Record what a visible obstacle looks like.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Compare a short exchange in [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) with its matching moment in the [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI); name the obstacle shown on screen.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Add two more field notes to your writing document. Describe only what a camera could capture; do not archive these routine notes in the Session Vault.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Check that both observations have a specific action, not just a mood.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Practise consonants and vowels from memory (10m), then write and read 15 syllable blocks (50m).

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Study [Anatomy of a Screenplay](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6PLSJBTzaGw) on short, present-tense action lines. Rewrite three vague sentences as filmable movements.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: In [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) and the [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI), find one object that helps communicate a character's situation. Note the exact difference.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Add two field notes to your writing document. Include one revealing object or gesture in each; keep the notes out of the Session Vault.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Separate "what I saw" from "what I think it means" in both entries.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Study the final consonant (batchim) using 집, 밥, 산. Pronounce and copy each, then test 7 familiar blocks.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Study [How to Write Great Scenes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TukzX6R57Y) on character (08:21–12:42). Identify how choices reveal a possible want.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Read a Miles-and-family moment in [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) and watch it in the [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI); describe one choice the film makes visible.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Add two final field notes to your writing document, completing ten. Choose the three with the clearest visible conflict; do not archive the raw notes in the Session Vault.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Count all ten; improve the two entries with the vaguest visual details.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Read 나무, 바다, 모자, 사람, 가방; copy each 3 times and sound out all syllables.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Watch [How to Write a Logline](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pMj8xUa1jOA). Write down protagonist + desire + obstacle, and one example logline.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: From [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) and the [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI), identify a character's want and one obstacle using a specific action as evidence.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: From the observation bank, write THREE different one-sentence film premises. Underline the goal and obstacle in each; select the strongest.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Choose one premise that can support a clear decision in a 3–5-page short. Record why in two sentences.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Write Hangul vowels and consonants from memory; read 10 mixed words; correct mistakes.

days.title: Sat 17 Oct · Day 7 · Saturday Director's Challenge

tasks.label: Find the visual idea · 25m
tasks.text: Revisit one short dialogue-free moment in the [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI). Identify how action, silence, or framing communicates intention.

tasks.label: Silent-scene challenge · 50m
tasks.text: Choose an observation. Write a **one-page fictional scene without dialogue**: someone wants an object or outcome, meets resistance, and makes a decision. Use only visible actions.

tasks.label: Direct the scene · 30m
tasks.text: Draw **six numbered frames** for your scene. Under each, specify what we see and why that angle is needed. No filming required.

tasks.label: Finish · 15m
tasks.text: Read the scene beside the drawings. Remove one shot that repeats information, then save both under "Saturday Silent Scene".

days.title: Sun 18 Oct · Day 8 · Sunday Studio Day

tasks.label: Story choice · 45m
tasks.text: Select Friday's strongest premise. Write its character, want, obstacle, turning point, and possible ending in five separate sentences.

tasks.label: Write a scene · 90m
tasks.text: Create **one original 1–2-page formatted screenplay scene**. Show the character encountering resistance and choosing a new tactic. Save as "Scene Packet — Scene 1".

tasks.label: Director's boards · 60m
tasks.text: Draw **eight shot frames** for the written scene. Mark each subject's position and which action prompts a cut. Optional: test two framings at home with your phone.

tasks.label: Read and revise · 45m
tasks.text: Read the scene aloud; cut at least three unnecessary explanations; check that the scene changes the situation. Save v1 and name the next scene.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Practise ㅐ and ㅔ, read 10 mixed syllables, then make a simple four-sentence self-introduction. Take short breaks during the studio session.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Study [How to Write Great Scenes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TukzX6R57Y) on how a character's action can contradict what they say.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Compare a script line in [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) with actor behavior in the [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI); note one unstated emotion or intention.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: In your Scene Packet, write **Scene 2 (1 page)**: a character tries to conceal something; another notices a conflicting detail.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Label the moment where a viewer could draw an inference, rather than directly knowing the character's motive.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Practice 저는... and 은/는 in five short true sentences, then read them aloud.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Study [Anatomy of a Screenplay](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6PLSJBTzaGw) on concise filmable verbs. Rewrite three sentences of vague description.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Study the timing of a pause or glance in [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) and the matching [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI) moment. Write what the script does and does not specify.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Write **Scene 3 (about 1 page)** without dialogue. Include a request, rejection and changed tactic shown through actions.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Check that each action can be photographed without voiceover explaining motives.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Review Hangul consonant–vowel pairing; read 10 one- or two-block words and note mistakes.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Study [How to Write Great Scenes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TukzX6R57Y), blocking section (16:25 onward). Note how physical placement changes a conversation.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Find one two-character interaction in [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) and [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI); sketch their positions before and after.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Write **Scene 4 (about 1 page)**: a misunderstanding forces someone to make a visible decision.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Read all four scenes and write one-line start and end states for each.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Learn introductory 이에요/예요; make five short self-introduction sentences.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Review [How to Write Great Scenes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TukzX6R57Y) on plot function (12:42–16:25): what changes between a scene's start and end?

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Locate a scene turn in [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) and its matching [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI) sequence. Record the event that changes the situation.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Revise Scenes 1–2 in your **same Scene Packet**. Cut five unnecessary lines and sharpen the obstacle.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Save the original and revised versions; write one reason each rewrite is clearer.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Review five familiar nouns and 은/는, then read and correct six simple Korean sentences.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Study [Anatomy of a Screenplay](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6PLSJBTzaGw) on action, dialogue and scene headings; correct formatting in one of your scenes.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Compare one written dialogue exchange from [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) with delivery and shot timing in [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI).

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Revise Scenes 3–4 and combine all four scenes into **one scene packet**. Choose the strongest scene to develop into a complete short.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Write why that one scene can support a beginning, middle and ending; save the packet.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Read 10 known words and record a 30-second Korean self-introduction; correct two mistakes.

days.title: Sat 24 Oct · Day 14 · Saturday Director's Challenge

tasks.label: Director's shot challenge · 25m
tasks.text: Pick one scene from your scene packet and name the precise moment where power or attention changes.

tasks.label: Stage six shots · 40m
tasks.text: Draw a **six-shot shooting plan**. For each: framing, character movement, and new information shown. Use your home as the possible location.

tasks.label: Camera experiment · 40m
tasks.text: OPTION A: With a phone at home, shoot 30–60 seconds of hands, an object and a reaction—no actors required. OPTION B: Draw eight detailed frames and note sound cues. Choose ONE option.

tasks.label: Assess · 15m
tasks.text: Compare your test to the written scene. Identify one unnecessary shot and one missing action. Save "Saturday Camera Lab".

days.title: Sun 25 Oct · Day 15 · Sunday Studio Day

tasks.label: Outline the whole film · 45m
tasks.text: Use the best scene from your packet. Write five beats: setup → disruption → escalation → choice → consequence. Keep the story possible to film in one or two locations.

tasks.label: Write the complete screenplay · 90m
tasks.text: Draft an **original 3–5-page screenplay** with INT./EXT., visible present-tense action and a complete ending. Finish the story before polishing any single paragraph.

tasks.label: Rewrite for visual storytelling · 45m
tasks.text: Read it aloud. Replace at least three explanatory lines with filmable behavior; check that every scene changes something.

tasks.label: Plan the filmed sequence · 60m
tasks.text: Draw **six shots** for the climactic choice, indicating subject, camera position and what the audience learns. Save the screenplay as v1 and boards in the same working project.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Review the vocabulary and particles learned so far. Write five short sentences and practise one-minute self-introduction. Take breaks between filmmaking blocks.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Revisit [How to Write Great Scenes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TukzX6R57Y) on scene conflict and choices. Create a three-question checklist for your own draft.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: From [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) and [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI), compare how an opening quickly establishes an audience question.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Open Sunday's script. Rewrite its first page so the character's goal and immediate problem become visible sooner.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Save v2 and note the single clearest improvement.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Learn three common Korean action verbs; say and write five short sentences using known vocabulary.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Study [Anatomy of a Screenplay](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6PLSJBTzaGw) on present-tense action and dialogue. Highlight one overly explanatory paragraph in your draft.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Find a scene in [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) and [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI) where gesture or sound replaces explanation. Note the exact substitution.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Revise your short screenplay's **action lines and dialogue**: shorten five lines, then add one precise gesture where needed.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Read the revised scene aloud and remove redundant explanation. Save a dated revision.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Review the verbs from yesterday; practise introductory -아요/-어요 and produce five short examples.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Study [How to Write Great Scenes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TukzX6R57Y) on plot and staging. Identify one cause-and-effect link in the climactic choice.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Compare the turning point in a script scene from [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) with screen timing in [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI).

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Check the short screenplay's ending: give the protagonist a choice and show its consequence. Revise the final half-page, then update your six-shot storyboard.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Make sure the story has a beginning, turn and ending; save the next draft.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Listen to a short beginner Korean audio clip twice; write five words or phrases you recognize.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Review [Anatomy of a Screenplay](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6PLSJBTzaGw) on screenplay formatting, focusing on headings, action and character/dialogue placement.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Choose an opening sequence in [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) and the [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI). Note one instance where the finished film adds visual or sound information.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Give your 3–5-page screenplay one complete read. If possible ask one trusted reader **"What does the protagonist want, and what changes?"** Otherwise perform the same test yourself.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Fix the two biggest clarity problems and save a new draft; do not start a new story.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Read a six-line beginner Korean passage, identify known words and practise pronunciation.

tasks.label: Theory · 30m
tasks.text: Review the [Anatomy of a Screenplay](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6PLSJBTzaGw) lesson and write five screenplay-format rules you can now apply.

tasks.label: Script → film · 30m
tasks.text: Compare one last 1–3-page excerpt of [Sony screenplay](https://origin-flash.sonypictures.com/ist/awards_screenplays/SV_screenplay.pdf) with the exact corresponding [official opening clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zzH4rV08TLI) moment; note your strongest directing lesson.

tasks.label: Create · 40m
tasks.text: Proofread the **finished 3–5-page short screenplay**, save the editable file and export a PDF. Keep your four-scene packet and six-shot plan.

tasks.label: Review · 20m
tasks.text: Check that the observation bank has ten real entries. Record three improvements for Month 2 and one scene-writing weakness to practise.

tasks.label: Korean · 60m
tasks.text: Test Hangul and 15 familiar syllable blocks or words, then speak a one-minute self-introduction and correct mistakes.
